brief.scope: Read ../in/watchdog-implementation-findings.md WHOLE. Independently adjudicate the two concrete integration findings against current watchdog.py and its proposed efficiency contract, with safe isolated probes. Inspect the bounded efficiency properties for additional real defects. Return UPHELD/PARTIAL/REJECTED findings in the review envelope. No implementation/tests, broad suites, real-store mutations, vendor/GitHub calls. Do not claim suite green proves the new boundaries.

findings.claim: UPHELD candidate P2 A: held_matches memory-maps a mutable regular file then regex-searches the mapping; truncating that file after mmap delivers SIGBUS (child exit -7, empty stderr) instead of a Python exception, so the tick guard never runs and the loop does not outlive the input error. A bounded pread/streaming reader is the necessary correction: the same truncate after fstat+pread returned zero bytes and exited 0. CPython 3.12 makes Pattern.search read-only, so the candidate's injected-search recipe does not run here; wrapping mmap.mmap inside held_matches reproduces the same SIGBUS. launch.py opens raw.out with wb (truncate) on a non-resume attempt, which is a real truncate window against a live mapping.

UPHELD candidate P2 B: entries() calls input_fingerprint() outside the per-record OSError handler, and fingerprint only swallows FileNotFoundError. A permission or ENOTDIR failure on one job's watched input raises out of entries(); Watch.__init__ stores it as startup_error so the armed line says unreachable closed records ignored; --once then prints one watchdog error and classifies no later record. Contrast: record.json as a directory is caught per-record and scanning continues, including deviation errors on a sibling closed job. Isolated chmod 000 on a job directory and a PermissionError monkeypatch on stderr.stat reproduced the same abort. Error entries are not cached as success; amended and resumed closed records do invalidate. Store-directory enumeration failure still reaches the tick guard.

Additional: ERROR_BYTES_RE is the old Unicode ERROR_TEXT_RE compiled as ASCII bytes, which does not preserve the pre-existing lexical deviation definitions. Measured: e-acute+errored is a bytes match and a text non-match; errors with NBSP before =2 is a text match and a bytes non-match; ASCII 'the tests errored' still matches both.

Additional: run() uses subprocess text=True and does not catch UnicodeDecodeError, so malformed non-UTF8 forge bytes never become the unavailable reading the efficiency contract requires. A local gh stub writing 0xff 0xfe made run() raise UnicodeDecodeError rather than return None; forge() therefore cannot label that output unreachable. JSON-shaped malformations already return None.

envelope.note: Candidate P2 A UPHELD; candidate P2 B UPHELD; no candidate REJECTED or PARTIAL. Inspected and holding: --forge-every schedule and cached/fresh heartbeat labels; 200+ page-full label; JSON malformed/unavailable forge readings stay unreachable; closed-record amend/resume cache invalidation; error entries not cached as success; startup parses record.json once; store iterdir failure reaches the tick guard. Existing test_watchdog.py has 56 test_ functions counted from source and was not executed; suite green is not proof of the new boundaries. No implementation or tests authored; no real-store mutation; no vendor/GitHub calls; probes confined to this job's out/.
